A header that shrinks and fades, a parallax image, a bar that fills in. Outside the range it holds at whichever end it reached, and with no scroll view above it, at the start.

params.name: key
params.doc: Names this widget within its screen or dialog. In a list, its state moves with its item when the list reorders; a new key is a fresh widget; `ui.focus` and `ui.scrollTo` find a widget by it.

params.name: from
params.doc: The scroll offset the effects start at.

params.name: to
params.doc: The scroll offset they finish at.

widgets.example: ListView(children: [ScrollTransition(from: 0, to: 160, effects: [{ effect: .fade, from: 1, to: 0 }, { effect: .slide, from: { x: 0, y: 0 }, to: { x: 0, y: -0.4 } }], child: SizedBox(height: 160, child: Center(child: Text(text: "Header", style: .headlineMedium)))), SizedBox(height: 900)])

widgets.name: AnimatedSwitcher
widgets.doc: Swaps one child for another with a transition between them. Give it a `value`: what the child is showing. When that changes, the child is a new one and the two cross over. (A `key` on the child cannot do this: rfw builds a child below the widget that was given it, so the switcher never sees the key.) The child on its way out is a live subtree, not a snapshot: it is still bound to the data it reads, so it shows the new values while it fades. Use this to bring something in and take something out, not to show two values of one thing at once.

params.name: key
params.doc: Names this widget within its screen or dialog. In a list, its state moves with its item when the list reorders; a new key is a fresh widget; `ui.focus` and `ui.scrollTo` find a widget by it.

params.name: value
params.doc: What the child is showing -- `data.tab`, `item.id`. A new one means a new child.

params.name: reverseDuration
params.doc: For the child on its way out.

params.name: switchOutCurve
params.doc: For the child on its way out.

widgets.example: AnimatedSwitcher(duration: 300, transition: .scale, value: "a", child: Icon(icon: .check_circle, size: 40, color: .primary))

widgets.name: BackdropFilter
widgets.doc: Blurs whatever is painted behind it -- frosted glass. In Flutter it blurs its whole layer, which without a clip is the screen; this one clips to its own bounds, so a 48-pixel bar blurs a 48-pixel bar. `borderRadius` makes that clip a rounded one, and `clip: false` gives Flutter's own behaviour back. The clip is also what bounds the cost: this is the most expensive widget in Flutter. A `child` is painted over the blur, so a glass panel is this with a translucent Container inside it. Several of them over one background should sit in a `BackdropGroup` with `grouped: true`, which reads the background once for all of them instead of once each.

params.name: key
params.doc: Names this widget within its screen or dialog. In a list, its state moves with its item when the list reorders; a new key is a fresh widget; `ui.focus` and `ui.scrollTo` find a widget by it.

params.name: blur
params.doc: The blur radius on both axes.

params.name: blurX
params.doc: Overrides `blur` across.

params.name: blurY
params.doc: Overrides `blur` down.

params.name: tileMode
params.doc: What is sampled past the edge.

params.name: borderRadius
params.doc: Makes the clip a rounded rectangle.

params.name: clip
params.doc: Clips the blur to this widget. False blurs the whole layer, as Flutter does.

params.name: blendMode
params.doc: How the blurred backdrop meets what is under it.

params.name: grouped
params.doc: Share one read of the backdrop with the other filters in the enclosing BackdropGroup.

params.name: child
params.doc: Painted over the blur.

widgets.example: Stack(children: [Container(width: 220, height: 140, decoration: { gradient: { type: .linear, colors: [.primary, .tertiary] } }), Positioned(left: 20, top: 40, width: 180, height: 60, child: BackdropFilter(blur: 14, borderRadius: .lg, child: Container(decoration: { color: "surface/40", borderRadius: .lg }, child: Center(child: Text(text: "Frosted")))))])

widgets.name: BackdropGroup

params.name: key

widgets.name: ClipPath
widgets.doc: Clips its child to a shape: a `shape` (`.stadium`, `.circle`, a map), or `path`, SVG path data in a `viewBox` scaled to fit as `CustomPaint` scales its shapes. With neither it is simply its child.

widgets.name: Dismissible
widgets.doc: A row that is swiped away. `background` shows behind it on the way out, and `secondaryBackground` when it goes the other way. `onDismissed` fires with `{ direction }` once it has gone, and the row is then out of the tree: take it out of your data there, or it comes back on the next rebuild. Give it a `key` that belongs to the row, so the right one goes.

params.name: key
params.doc: Names this widget within its screen or dialog. In a list, its state moves with its item when the list reorders; a new key is a fresh widget; `ui.focus` and `ui.scrollTo` find a widget by it.

params.name: direction
params.doc: Which way it may be swiped.

params.name: background
params.doc: Behind it as it goes start-to-end.

params.name: secondaryBackground
params.doc: Behind it as it goes end-to-start.

params.name: onDismissed
params.doc: Receives `{ direction }`.

params.name: dismissThreshold
params.doc: How far across it must go, as a fraction of its width.

params.name: resizeDuration
params.doc: How long the gap takes to close. Null leaves no gap.

widgets.example: SizedBox(height: 90, child: ListView(children: [Dismissible(key: "one", background: ColoredBox(color: .errorContainer), child: ListTile(title: "Swipe me away"))]))

types.Widget|String: A widget, or a string as shorthand for `Text(text: ...)`.
types.Widget|Icon: A widget, or an icon name as shorthand for `Icon(icon: ...)`.
types.List<Widget>: A list of widgets: `[ Text(text: "a"), Text(text: "b") ]`, `...for item in data.items: ...` included.
types.String: A string: `"hello"`. A name may be written with a dot instead of quotes: `.center` is `"center"`.
types.Key: A string or number: `"email"`, `item.id`, or a list joined into one: `["row-", item.id]`.
types.value: Any rfw value -- a string, number or bool -- compared by equality.
types.Spacing: A number, or a spacing token from the theme: `"xs"`, `"sm"`, `"md"` (or `.md`), `"lg"`, `"xl"`.
types.Color: An ARGB int (`0xFF6750A4`), a colour-scheme role (`"primary"`, or with a dot, `.onSurfaceVariant`), a theme colour (`"divider"`), a custom token (`"success"`), `"#RRGGBB"`, or any of those with an opacity in percent: `"onSurface/60"`.
types.TextStyle: A text-theme name (`"titleLarge"` or `.titleLarge`, or a style the theme names), or a map. `{ base: "titleLarge", fontWeight: "bold", color: "primary" }` is `titleLarge.copyWith(...)`; keys: fontSize, fontWeight (`"bold"`, `600`), fontStyle, letterSpacing, wordSpacing, height, color, backgroundColor, decoration, decorationColor, decorationStyle, fontFamily, shadows, overflow.
types.EdgeInsets: A number or spacing token for every side, `[start, top, end, bottom]`, or `{ all, horizontal, vertical, top, bottom, start, end, left, right }`.
types.BorderRadius: A number or radius token (`"md"`, `"full"`) for every corner, or `{ all, top, bottom, start, end, topStart, topEnd, bottomStart, bottomEnd }`.
types.Decoration: `{ color, borderRadius, border, boxShadow, gradient, image, shape }`; `type: "shape"` takes `shape` as an outline instead.
types.ShapeBorder: `"stadium"`, `"circle"`, a number (a rounded rectangle of that radius), or `{ type: "rounded" | "stadium" | "circle" | "beveled" | "continuous" | "superellipse", borderRadius, side }`.
types.Border: One side for all four (`{ color, width }`) or `{ top, bottom, left, right }` / `{ start, end }`.
types.BoxShadow: `{ color, offset: { x, y }, blurRadius, spreadRadius }`.
types.Gradient: `{ type: "linear" | "radial" | "sweep", colors: [...], stops, begin, end, center, radius }`.
types.ButtonStyle: `{ backgroundColor, foregroundColor, overlayColor, iconColor, elevation, padding, minimumSize, fixedSize, side, shape, textStyle, ... }` -- each a value, or a map by state: `{ default: "primary", pressed: "primaryContainer", disabled: "outline" }`.
types.InputDecoration: `{ labelText, hintText, helperText, errorText, prefixIcon, suffixIcon, prefixText, suffixText, filled, fillColor, border, enabledBorder, focusedBorder, contentPadding, isDense, ... }`; icons may be names, borders `"outline"`, `"underline"`, `"none"` or `{ type, borderRadius, color, width }`.
types.IconData: A Material icon name (`"home"`, `.favorite_border`) or a Cupertino one with a prefix (`"cupertino.heart_fill"`, `.cupertino.heart_fill`).
types.Size: `{ width, height }`, `[width, height]`, or one number for a square.
types.BoxConstraints: `{ minWidth, maxWidth, minHeight, maxHeight }`, or `width` / `height` to pin an axis.
types.GridDelegate: `{ crossAxisCount, mainAxisSpacing, crossAxisSpacing, childAspectRatio, mainAxisExtent }`, or `maxCrossAxisExtent` in place of `crossAxisCount`.
types.Image: A URL (`"https://..."`) or an asset name.
types.Shape: `{ shape, ...its own keys, color, gradient, stroke, cap, join }`. shape: `.rect` (`rect: [x, y, w, h]`, `radius`), `.circle` (`center: [x, y]`, `radius`), `.line` (`from`, `to`), `.arc` (`center`, `radius`, `start` and `sweep` in degrees clockwise from three o'clock), `.path` (`d`: SVG path data, M L H V C S Q T Z; not arcs), `.text` (`text`, `at`, `style`). Filled unless it has a `stroke` width.
types.Effect: `{ effect, from, to, ...its own keys }`. effect: `.fade` (`from`, `to`: opacity), `.scale` (`from`, `to`, `alignment`), `.slide` (`from`, `to`: `{ x, y }` as fractions of the child's own size), `.rotate` (`from`, `to` in turns, `alignment`), `.blur` (`from`, `to`: sigma, `tileMode`), `.tint` (`from`, `to`: colours, `blendMode`), `.shimmer` (`color`, `width`, `angle` in turns). An effect nobody knows is left out.
types.Builder: A widget builder: `(size) => Text(text: size.breakpoint)`. The name is yours; `name.x` reads what the widget passes, which its own docs list.
types.ItemBuilder: Builds one row from its item: `(m) => ListTile(title: m.name)`. The name is yours; `m` is the item -- a map (`m.name`), a string or a number -- or, with `itemCount` and no `items`, the row's index. `args.*`, `data.*` and `state.*` still read as they do around it.

types.event<int>: A handler; an event receives `{ value: <int> }`.
types.event<double>: A handler; an event receives `{ value: <double> }`.
types.event<String>: A handler; an event receives `{ value: "<text>" }`.
types.event<value>: A handler; an event receives `{ value: <the selected value> }`.
types.event<Date>: A handler; an event receives `{ value: "<ISO date>" }`.
types.event<Range>: A handler; an event receives `{ start, end }`.
types.List<Map>: A list of maps; the parameter says which keys each takes.
types.Map: A map; the parameter says which keys it takes.
